title: Feature activation cadence & ownership rotor — KPI log
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a lightweight, repeatable cadence for feature activations and an explicit rotating ownership pattern (the 'ownership rotor') to keep KPI tracking, stakeholder signaling, and contingency decisions continuous and visible across launches. Goal: reduce decision friction during ramps and standardize who owns which runway signals each week.

Context / why we need this:
- Product ops receives ad-hoc requests during launches; context and ownership blur across oncall/product/support.
- Existing trackers are proliferating (sheets + decks) but we lack a single, weekly-signed checkpoint owner who can escalate.
- The rotor enforces a predictable owner-of-record for 7-day windows and ties them to SLA thresholds and rapid rollback/fallback triggers.

Core concepts (quick):
- Ownership rotor: 7-day owner-of-record who approves go/no-go escalations, triages metric anomalies, and coordinates cross-team fixes.
- Runway KPIs: a minimal set (token latency P50/P95, error rate, cost-per-1k-tokens, model-quality regression score, traffic success ratio).
- Signal thresholds: green/yellow/red bands mapped to actions (auto-scale, rate-limit, rollback).
- Decision friction log: short freeform notes capturing unresolved decisions, blocker owners, and immediate mitigation steps.

Runway KPI table (canonical minimal set) — update weekly in sheet, owner signs off in comments:
- Active requests/min: baseline + uplift%
- P50 latency (ms) and P95 latency (ms)
- 5xx rate (% of requests)
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD)
- Quality pass rate (evals on canaries, %)
- Cache hit ratio (prefix / KV)
- Canary divergence score (text/rouge-like metric)

Signal bands and actions (examples):
- GREEN: within expected range. No action beyond monitoring.
- YELLOW: sustained 10–20% deviation for 15+ minutes. Owner initiates mitigation plan (throttle, enable cache, add workers). Notify SRE + infra runbook.
- RED: >20% deviation or customer-impacting errors. Owner executes fallback policy (route to variant model, reduce rollout, roll back). Pager escalation if >30 mins.

Ownership rotor (example schedule and responsibilities):
- Week A (Mon 00:00 — Sun 23:59): Maya Chen (product-ops) — primary: KPI signoff, stakeholder updates, gate decisions, coordinate SRE.
- Week B: Evan Brooks (product-ops) — primary: capacity tuning, slas review, billing ops note.
- Week C: Sofia Patel (customer-success liaison) — primary: customer comms, support escalations.
- Week D: Liam O'Neill (platform) — primary: infra fallbacks, autoscale overrides.
Notes: rotor cycles every 4 weeks for larger launches; for small pilots we use 1-week cycles only. Owner rotates proactively when a high-severity incident begins.

Weekly checklist for the owner-of-record (to be completed in the tracker):
- [ ] Pull last 7-day KPI snapshot and compare to baseline (attach chart link).
- [ ] Confirm canary pass/fail status and include sample prompt/response mismatches.
- [ ] Run the lightweight regression eval on a fixed prompt set (link to eval run).
- [ ] Confirm cost delta vs forecast and note any budget breach risks.
- [ ] Post a short decision note in the Decision Friction Log (2–4 bullets).
- [ ] If any signal in YELLOW/RED, open an incident/ops channel and tag SRE lead + platform owner.
- [ ] Complete handoff notes for next week owner and mark any lingering actions.

Decision friction log (format to paste into tracker):
- Timestamp | Owner | Short problem statement | Immediate mitigation | Blockers / next actions | Jira/Confluence links
Example:
- 2025-02-02 10:12 | Maya Chen | P95 spikes to 2200ms after 10k users | Enabled cache warmup + reduced batch size | Waiting on infra to scale GPUs (JIRA-OPS-1283) | https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/activation-guidelines

Escalation ladder (compact):
- Owner-of-record -> Product Ops Lead -> SRE Manager -> Platform Director -> Exec on-call (if >90 mins and customer-impacting).

Templates / quick links (to copy into trackers):
- Owner weekly signoff comment template: "Week of YYYY-MM-DD — KPIs checked, canary status PASS/FAIL, cost change +/-, open items: []"
- Incident channel starter: "Activation incident: feature X, owner Y, symptom: [brief], immediate mitigation: [brief], link to KPI dashboard: [url]"

Open questions / follow-ups (to resolve before GA):
- Should rotor owners have a small on-call compensation or swap credit? (ops compensation policy required)
- Define exact quality-pass metric (currently a placeholder 'eval pass %') — product-research to propose by 2025-02-18.
- Auto-escalation thresholds for billing surprises (cost per 1k tokens threshold) — finance input needed.

Immediate next actions (owner: Maya Chen):
- Convert this working doc into the product-ops canonical tracker (sheet) and populate the last 8 weeks of baseline KPIs. (Due 2025-02-09)
- Add a simple script to snapshot KPIs and post to the tracker every morning (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/activation-scripts/pull/221)
- Align with SRE on the exact names for metrics and chart IDs used on the dashboard.

If you are picking up next week as owner: please read the last 3 Decision Friction Log entries and sign the weekly signoff in the tracker by Tue 09:00 PT.
